label: read-bm-making
in_my_words: They want to build a thin plastic strip made of two layers that curls when it gets damp, a bit like a leaf curling. The idea is a window shade that moves on its own with the humidity, no motor needed. Before building anything they first have to soak test strips and measure how much the plastics swell, because nobody has published that.
how_in_my_words: They print flat strips from different resins, rinse and dry them until the weight stops dropping, and measure their size. Then they soak the strips and weigh and measure them again to see how much they swell. Next they stick a swelling layer on a non-swelling layer, wet it, photograph the curl, and fit a circle to get the bend. Finally they compare the real bend with what an old formula from 1925 predicts. They bet it will land within a fifth of the prediction.

test_questions.question: Why does the two-layer strip bend?
test_questions.my_answer: One layer swells when wet and the other barely does, so the strip curves.

test_questions.question: What is the first thing they must measure and why?
test_questions.my_answer: How much each plastic swells, because no one has published that number.

test_questions.question: What result would show they are wrong?
test_questions.my_answer: A curl far outside 28 to 83 mm radius, or plastic that swells too little to see.

test_questions.question: Does the bend rule prove real plastic will behave that way?
test_questions.my_answer: No. The checks only show the maths is consistent.

test_questions.question: What will the shade be made of and how big will the first real one be?
test_questions.my_answer: Cannot tell exactly; the text mentions a small window-shade module but gives no size or design.

sentences_i_could_not_follow: The rule assumes a perfect bond and small bends, and the real strip may break those assumptions.
Last line: VERDICT: the ceiling holds in every check; grid maximum 1.499998 at m^2 n = 0.99996
We found no part checked against a proof-assistant-checked law, but that is a search result, not proof.
Claim that all Form 4 resins are acrylates and that no bond data exists: left out, because only 14 safety sheets were checked and the rest is a negative.
A 0.4 millimetre layer would settle in hours to about a day. A louver blade might take 1 to 10 days. Both rest on an assumed slab thickness.
what_would_help: Start with a single plain sentence on the goal and a simple picture of the bending strip, and cut the jargon (proof assistant, ceiling, t90). Explain why humid air matters when the tests soak in liquid water, and say what the shade would actually look like.
